defects: Does not use the actual restriction functor (resFunctor/Rep.res); C_restricted is an independent parameter not constrained to equal S.map(resFunctor f), so the theorem doesn't actually express 'restrict along f' as a functorial operation

Redefines exactness as (map₂ ∘ map₁ = 0 ∧ Injective map₁ ∧ Surjective map₂), i.e. a short exact sequence, which is strictly stronger than the general ShortComplex.Exact notion (im = ker at the middle object) used in gold — changes the mathematical content of 'exact'

Uses raw Representation H R / Representation G R with a bare .ρ field and unbundled linear maps instead of the bundled Rep k G category objects and morphisms used in gold, so equivariance of map₁/map₂ must be smuggled in as extra hypotheses rather than being part of the morphism structure

Adds four extraneous antecedent hypotheses (equivariance of C.map₁, C.map₂ under H, and of C_restricted.map₁, C_restricted.map₂ under G) that are not part of the original statement and are stated as implications preceding the iff rather than as a clean biconditional, obscuring whether this is a well-formed single proposition

The linking between C and C_restricted is only via ad hoc mixed conditions like C_restricted.map₁.comp (C.X₁.ρ (φ g)) = (C.X₂.ρ (φ g)).comp C_restricted.map₁, which conflates the two complexes' representation spaces instead of stating C_restricted is literally the image of C under a restriction functor

Drops the general ring/semiring generality structure of gold (k a commutative ring, general categorical Exact) in favor of a hand-rolled injective/surjective condition tied to Function.Injective/Function.Surjective on modules
